CC15_LETTER_INCORRECT: Your name letter in {cell} should be {expected}, from your name, but it shows {found}. Double-check it against how your name is spelled.
CC16_COUNTRY_BLANK: Your country in {cell} is blank. Choose a country from the approved list on this tab.
CC16_COUNTRY_NOT_APPROVED: Your country in {cell} ('{found}') isn't on the approved country list. Choose a country from the list on this tab, spelled the same way.
CC16_COUNTRY_WRONG_INITIAL: Your country in {cell}, {country}, doesn't start with {expected_letter}, the letter above it in row 15. Choose a country that starts with {expected_letter}.
CC17_DATE_MISSING: Your rate lookup date in {cell} is missing. Enter the date you looked up the rate, as MM/DD/YYYY.
CC17_DATE_TOO_OLD: Your rate lookup date in {cell} ({date}) is {age_days} days away. It should be within {max_days} days, so enter the date you actually looked up the rate.
CC17_DATE_PARSE_ERROR: Your rate lookup date in {cell} isn't a date Excel recognizes. Enter it as MM/DD/YYYY.
CC18_COUNTRY_UNKNOWN: Your currency code in {cell} ({found}) couldn't be checked because the country above it in row 16 is blank or not on the approved list. Fix the country first, then enter its code.
CC18_COUNTRY_UNKNOWN_BLANK: Your currency code in {cell} is blank, and the country above it in row 16 is blank or not on the approved list. Choose an approved country, then enter its 3-letter currency code.
CC18_CODE_INCORRECT: Your currency code for {country} in {cell} should be {expected}, but it shows {found}.
CC19_API_FETCH_FAILED: [MANUAL REVIEW] Live exchange rates could not be fetched ({error}), so the rates in C19:F19 were not checked. Please verify them by hand.
CC19_CODE_MISSING: Your exchange rate in {rate_cell} couldn't be checked because there's no currency code in {code_cell}. Enter the 3-letter code first.
CC19_CODE_INVALID: Your currency code in {code_cell} ({code}) isn't one we could look up, so its exchange rate couldn't be checked. Use the 3-letter code for the country in row 16.
CC19_RATE_NOT_NUMERIC: Your exchange rate in {rate_cell} is blank or isn't a plain number. Type in the rate you looked up as a number, like 17.235.
CC19_RATE_OUTSIDE_TOLERANCE: Your exchange rate in {rate_cell} isn't within 5% of the current rate (about {true_rate} per US dollar). Double-check the rate you looked up.
CC19_FORMAT_BAD: Your exchange rate in {rate_cell} should show 3 decimal places (Number format 0.000).
CC20_FORMULA_MISSING: Your budget in the foreign currency ({cell}) needs a formula. Multiply your budget by the exchange rate: =B4*{rate_ref}.
CC20_FORMULA_TEXT: Your budget in the foreign currency ({cell}) turns the answer into text ({found}), so Excel can't calculate with it. Keep it a number, =B4*{rate_ref}, and show the currency code with number formatting instead.
CC20_FORMULA_BAD: Your budget in the foreign currency ({cell}) isn't calculating correctly. It should multiply your budget by the exchange rate: {expected_a}.
CC20_FORMULA_PARTIAL: Your budget in the foreign currency ({cell}) multiplies, but uses typed-in numbers instead of cell references. Use {expected_a} so it updates if the budget or rate changes.
CC20_FORMAT_BAD: Your budget in the foreign currency ({cell}) should be formatted with 2 decimals and its currency code, {expected_code}, not a $ sign.
CC21_FORMULA_MISSING: Your conversion back to US dollars ({cell}) needs a formula. Divide D4 by the exchange rate: {expected}.
CC21_FORMULA_BAD: Your conversion back to US dollars ({cell}) should divide D4 by the exchange rate: {expected}. Right now it's {found}.
CC21_FORMAT_BAD: Your conversion back to US dollars ({cell}) should be formatted as Currency ($) with 2 decimals.
CC21_FORMULA_PARTIAL: Your conversion back to US dollars ({cell}) divides D4, but not by the right rate cell. Use {expected} instead of {found}.
CC17_DATE_YEAR_TYPO: Your rate lookup date in {cell} ({date}) was accepted, but the year looks like a typo for {year}. Fix the year so it matches your other dates.
CC17_DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE: Your rate lookup date in {cell} ({date}) doesn't look right. It should be on or before the day you saved the file ({saved}) and within {max_age} days of it, so enter the date you actually looked up the rate.
CC17_DATE_INCONSISTENT: Your rate lookup date in {cell} ({date}) is {off_by} days away from your other dates. All four rates should be looked up around the same time, within {max_days} days of each other.
